title: Behind Nvidia's Earnings: AI Bubble Fueled by Debt and Circular Financing
dek: Nvidia's stunning results depend on a few customers and circular financing; whether the AI bubble can last hinges on the debt market staying open forever.
why: This monologue exposes the circular financing and debt dependence behind Nvidia's earnings, which is essential for understanding the nature of the AI bubble.
who: Investors and entrepreneurs focused on the AI bubble and tech stock valuations, as well as anyone wanting to understand the risks behind Nvidia's business model.

points.body: Nvidia's earnings show staggering revenue, but 16% comes from a single unnamed customer, and 44% of revenue comes from three customers. Of its accounts receivable, 70% comes from five companies, and it offers investment-grade customers payment terms of up to a year. This concentration means Nvidia's boom rests on continued purchases by a few giants; if they cut spending, results would plummet.

Nvidia's main customers, including hyperscalers, rely on debt because of soaring GPU costs. New cloud companies like CoreWeave and Nebius are rated investment-grade by rating agencies solely because their contracts come from creditworthy firms. Nvidia even offers payment terms from 90 days to a year, further tying itself to customers' debt positions.

points.h: Nvidia spreads money around with investments
points.body: Nvidia invested $6 billion in Poolside, acquired Hugging Face for nearly $13 billion, and is reportedly investing in Perplexity, Stargate, and others. Most of these targets are loss-making AI companies. Nvidia seems to be using investments to maintain the illusion of a thriving AI ecosystem, preventing any one company from collapsing and bursting the bubble.

Nvidia's CFO denies circular financing, but numerous deals show money circulating among Nvidia, its customers, and its investment targets. Morgan Stanley says Nvidia has become a 'balance sheet as a service' company, with commitments exceeding $366 billion. Nvidia both sells GPUs and leases them back; such contradictory operations raise questions about the authenticity of demand.

points.h: Jensen Huang claims AGI has been achieved
points.body: Jensen Huang claimed on the earnings call that the world has achieved AGI, but Ed believes this has not happened and should not be downplayed by the media. Such statements contrast sharply with Nvidia's financial maneuvers, highlighting the disconnect between AI hype and reality.

Nvidia's CFO projects 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028 to $674 billion, which would require existing customers to significantly increase orders and new cloud companies to take on more debt. CoreWeave already pays interest rates above 9%, and the entire system would need over a trillion dollars in debt to sustain—this is nearly impossible to continue.

Bloomberg reports that the so-called $500 billion AI data center fund has no actual source; it's just Nvidia announcing that asset management companies will invest, with the figure having no basis. Hyperscaler spending depends on Anthropic and OpenAI's promised $400 billion in GPU leases; if those promises fail, cloud revenue would evaporate by over 30%.

Nvidia invests in all AI companies to prevent any one from collapsing and undermining the 'AI revolution' narrative. No one panics now only because nothing has gone wrong yet, but everything depends on unlimited resources continuing. When the debt market tightens, the music stops.

quotes.text: The Groundhog once again saw its shadow with Nvidia reporting record earnings, continuing to inflate an ever more dangerous AI bubble with $96 billion worth of revenue and 16% of that coming from a single unnamed customer.
While Nvidia is unquestionably profitable and thriving revenue-wise, it's only doing so because of a few companies who are willing to be fin-dommed by Jensen Huang
NVIDIA is now a balance sheet as a service company with over $366 billion in commitments

Huang also claimed on an analyst call that the world has already achieved artificial general intelligence, which he defines as the ultimate form of the technology where the machines can think and act for themselves.
that announcement was literally just NVIDIA saying that a group of asset managers would invest half a trillion dollars in AI data centers, and that number, and I quote, had no obvious provenance.
Everything comes down to whether near-infinite resources are available for AI in perpetuity, and when those resources slow or stop, so too will the music.
